title: Stale unreachable rate-limit calls break lint in the owned auth module

evidence.quote:
from app.core.auth import (
    create_access_token,
    generate_api_token,
    get_token_prefix,
    hash_api_token,
    hash_password,
    verify_api_token,
    verify_password,

reasoning: The owned file contains two unreachable calls after a return, and both reference `request`, which is not defined in `revoke_api_token`. The same lint run reports F821 for both lines, and also reports F401 for the unused `verify_api_token` import. Even though the bad calls are after a return, Pyflakes still fails the configured lint check, blocking release.
reproduction: Run `python -m ruff check --no-cache app/api/auth.py`; Ruff reports F821 at lines 338 and 339 and F401 at line 17.
recommendation: Remove the unreachable `check_auth_rate_limit(request)` lines and remove the unused `verify_api_token` import, or wire rate limiting intentionally before authentication work with a real `Request` parameter if that behavior is required.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature has no linked tests, and runtime tests of GET /tokens would not execute unreachable code after a return or detect an unused import.
suggestedRegressionTest: Keep `ruff check .` in CI so undefined names and stale imports in route modules fail before release.
minimumFixScope: Clean up the dead lines at the end of `revoke_api_token` and the unused import in `app/api/auth.py`.
